title: Open and closed derived module inverse images jointly detect isomorphisms
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring and Lambda_T = p_T^* Lambda. Let i : Z -> X be a closed immersion and j : U -> X a quasi-compact open immersion with range(j) equal to the complement of range(i). In the unbounded derived category of Lambda_X-module objects on X_proet, let phi : K -> Kprime be a morphism. If Lj^*(phi) and Li^*(phi), using the total left derived module inverse images, are isomorphisms, then phi is an isomorphism. No boundedness or constructibility assumption is made. The coefficient categories and functors are those of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

source.place: (2) Isomorphism; open-closed detection after exact inverse images

proof.text: A module M whose open inverse image is zero has underlying abelian sheaf supported on the closed complement. Use the existing profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso to identify the underlying inverse image, and the abelian closed-support theorem to make its abelian adjunction unit invertible. Apply the existing private helper moduleUnitOfAbelian from Sheaf.Paper.CondensedOpenClosedRecollement (import all) to obtain invertibility of the module adjunction unit M -> i_*i^*M. If the closed inverse image is also zero then its direct image is zero, and consequently M is zero. The helper transports the abelian unit through the coefficient isomorphism; no duplicate unit-lifting theorem is introduced.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism; open-closed detection on each cohomology object

proof.text: The two module inverse images are exact. If both images of a module morphism are isomorphisms, exactness makes both restrictions of its kernel and cokernel zero. Step 1 makes that kernel and cokernel zero; the morphism is mono and epi, hence invertible in the abelian module category.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism; exact inverse images detect kernels and cokernels

proof.text: The levelwise derived exact inverse images commute with every homology object. The abelian joint-isomorphism detection therefore passes to the unbounded derived categories. The canonical isomorphisms from total left derived inverse image to levelwise exact inverse image transport this criterion to Lj^* and Li^*. This applies equally when the open or closed part is empty.
